issues.basis: Contract NL-CONTRACT-REF-023 (NL10, property=state_retention, state=Approaching). FCSTM: state:Approaching:line:14 with outgoing transitions line:21 (Arrived_Stop_SendArrived) and line:24 (Obstacle_Detected), both unguarded. No trace facts available to verify retention under a specific scenario.
issues.expected: The system must remain in Approaching while the 'nearing destination' condition holds; exits should only occur when ready to stop or decelerate.
issues.observed: Approaching (state:Approaching:line:14) has two outgoing transitions: transition:line:21 (Arrived_Stop_SendArrived -> [*]) and transition:line:24 (Obstacle_Detected -> [*]). Neither exit is guarded by a 'nearing destination' condition. The Obstacle_Detected exit could fire while the system is still nearing the destination, potentially violating the retention requirement. No trace scenario is available to confirm or refute the property.
issues.reason: The state_retention property requires that exits from Approaching only occur when the retention condition ceases to hold. The FCSTM has no guard on the Obstacle_Detected exit that would verify the 'nearing destination' condition has been resolved. Per routing discipline, state_retention contracts are preserved as predicate-null W1 when the downstream native binder may materialize a trace input.
issues.requirement_quote: The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The 'nearing destination' condition in the NL may be implicit in the Approaching state's identity (i.e., being in Approaching means you are nearing). Under this reading, the retention is satisfied trivially: the system is in Approaching by definition while nearing, and exits only when events fire that indicate stopping or emergency. The Obstacle_Detected exit could be argued to represent a higher-priority interrupt that overrides the retention.
issues.title: State retention in Approaching while nearing destination not verifiable

The 'Entry/Accelerate' text was parsed as trigger event Entry_Accelerate on the initial transition (line:15), not as a state action. semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL contract NL-CONTRACT-REF-023 states 'The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate.' The exact FCSTM facts show state:Approaching:line:14 has two unguarded outgoing transitions: transition:line:21 (Arrived_Stop_SendArrived to [*) and transition:line:24 (Obstacle_Detected to [*]). The source annotations at line 14 describe the state in terms of approaching and stopping behavior, which is compatible with both readings. No trace facts are available to resolve which reading the author intended, so the undercutting defeater survives.

decisions.reason: The NL contract NL-CONTRACT-REF-023 states 'The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate.' The exact FCSTM facts show state:Approaching:line:14 has two unguarded outgoing transitions: transition:line:21 (Arrived_Stop_SendArrived to [*) and transition:line:24 (Obstacle_Detected to [*]). The Obstacle_Detected exit can fire while the system is still nearing the destination, and it is not guarded by a condition verifying that the retention state has ceased. Under a strict reading of the NL, this violates retention because Obstacle_Detected is not one of the specified exit conditions ('ready to stop or decelerate'). However, a competent alternative reading holds that detecting an obstacle IS a form of being 'ready to stop' (emergency stop), making the unguarded safety exit an intentional design choice. The source annotations at line 14 describe the state in terms of approaching and stopping behavior, which is compatible with both readings. No trace facts are available to resolve which reading the author intended, so the undercutting defeater survives.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The Obstacle_Detected exit may represent a safety-priority interrupt that legitimately overrides the retention condition, since detecting an obstacle constitutes being 'ready to stop' in an emergency sense, making the unguarded exit an intentional design choice rather than a retention violation.
decisions.violated_obligation: The system must remain in the Approaching state while the 'nearing destination' condition holds; exits should only occur when ready to stop or decelerate, per NL contract NL10.
